reviews.body:
Reviewed the offset-aware scheduling fix and the follow-up test commit.

Behavior audit: a 42-cell matrix over schedule field, tz validity, and field combinations, plus a 90-cell superset, agree that exactly 7 cells change. All 7 are in the class where tz is not consumed (an offset-aware at, or every with a passed-over at/cron_expr). The two branches that actually read tz, the cron expression and a naive at, show zero change cell by cell. Re-running the same cells through the real CronService gives identical outcomes.

Mutation check on the final suite, each mutant applied to tool.py:
- M1 restore the base-wide tz precheck: 7 tests fail.
- M2 make the every branch reject at/cron: 4 tests fail.
- M3 make the every branch reject any invalid tz: 2 tests fail.
All three mutants stay red, so the tests carry the change and none survives.

Test counts: PR base 13, parent 15, prior head 19, now 23. Adjacent files 58, full cron 470. Ruff check and format are clean, and CI is green.

The new tests state what each pins: the valid-tz case pins field non-leakage and cannot distinguish the fix, the invalid-tz case pins tolerance, and the unparseable-at case pins the ISO error over the old timezone error. That split is honest and keeps both shapes.

No blockers. Merging.

comments.body:
## Windows compatibility review - PR #1404 @ 0c8f18dacb759dadcda7d1fbc21ab0829dcdf964

**Scope:** full PR diff against base 5218f8cb8e (2 files, +17/-18): the cron tool validates `tz` only where it is used - a `cron_expr`, or a naive `at` datetime - instead of also for `every` schedules and offset-aware `at` values, where it was ignored; the tests are parametrized to pin both sides.

**Result: no Windows compatibility issue found.** The behaviour change is a control-flow narrowing on in-memory schedule construction; no paths, quoting, subprocess, encoding or locking surface. `ZoneInfo(tz)` is the same call as before, only moved next to its use, and every failure still returns the same "unknown timezone" message. One platform note, unchanged by this PR: on Windows `zoneinfo` resolves IANA names through the `tzdata` package, which this environment has (the tests resolve `Asia/Shanghai`); a deployment without it would report every zone as unknown, exactly as it did before the change.

**Verification on this native Windows host** (Windows 11 26100; CPython from the shared venv; sparse partial clone pinned to 0c8f18dacb, paths `raven/`, `tests/`, `plugins-dist/`, `agents/`):

```
cd D:/tmp/g1404 && RVTREE='D:\tmp\g1404' PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=D:/tmp/pyc1404 PYTHONUTF8=1 \
  /d/projects/Raven/.venv/Scripts/python.exe -S /d/tmp/review-runner/runner.py \
  tests/test_cron_tool.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
-> 15 passed in 22.67s
```

The first checkout attempt failed on a network reset while fetching blobs (`RPC failed; curl 56`); a retry completed and the tree is the exact head commit.

**Gaps:** sparse partial clone rather than the whole repository; no live scheduler tick or DST transition was exercised.
